config.title: useOnlineStatus

intro.title: useOnlineStatus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component that displays whether the user's device is currently connected to the internet. You will learn to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to create a custom `useOnlineStatus` hook that tracks the browser's online and offline events. The main technologies involved are React hooks and the browser's `navigator.onLine` property and event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that updates the UI in real-time based on the network status.
intro.usecase: The useOnlineStatus hook is essential for building resilient applications that adapt to network conditions. In productivity apps like Google Docs or Figma, it triggers visual indicators when connectivity drops, preventing users from losing work. E-commerce platforms use it to disable checkout buttons and show offline messages when payment processing isn't possible. Developers implement this pattern in dashboards to pause real-time data updates and display cached content during network interruptions.

objectives: Implement the useOnlineStatus hook to detect network connectivity changes
Initialize state to track the browser's online status
Configure event listeners for online and offline events
Apply the hook in a React component to conditionally render UI elements
Manipulate component behavior based on network availability
Construct a cleanup function to remove event listeners
Integrate the custom hook with a user interface to display connectivity status

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: At the top of the file, import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a component named App that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Create a functional component named App that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize online status state
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, declare a state variable called isOnline using useState, initialized to true.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Call useState with the initial value true and destructure the returned array into isOnline and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a state variable isOnline initialized to true, ready to track online status.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState call that declares isOnline with initial value true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named isOnline with an initial value of true inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the App component, use useState to create a state variable called isOnline and set its initial value to true.

steps.title: Create the handleOnline function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named handleOnline that sets the isOnline state to true.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls the state setter function for isOnline with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleOnline function is defined and will update the online status to true when called.
successCriteria: A function named handleOnline is defined inside the App component and calls setIsOnline(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named handleOnline and calls setIsOnline(true).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleOnline function isn't defined correctly. It should be inside the App component and set isOnline to true.

steps.title: Create the handleOffline function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function called handleOffline that sets isOnline to false using the state setter.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsOnline with false as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleOffline function is defined inside the App component that updates the isOnline state to false.
successCriteria: The handleOffline function is defined and calls setIsOnline(false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your handleOffline function calls setIsOnline with false as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleOffline function should be defined inside the App component and set isOnline to false using setIsOnline.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: In your App component, replace the current return statement with a div element that has a className of 'app-container'.
steps.hint: Update the return statement to return a JSX div element with the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a div element with className 'app-container' as its main container.
successCriteria: The App component returns a JSX div element with className 'app-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div with exactly className='app-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to replace the return statement with a div element that has className='app-container'.

steps.title: Add the status indicator element
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add a div element that displays the current isOnline state value.
steps.hint: Use JSX to create a div element with the isOnline variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX
Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a div element containing the current online status value (true or false).
successCriteria: A div element is added inside the container div that displays the isOnline state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element inside the container div that shows the isOnline value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status indicator isn't displaying correctly. Check that you've added a div element with the isOnline variable inside curly braces.

steps.title: Add the Go Online button
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Go Online' inside the main container div, and wire its onClick event to call the handleOnline function.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with the text 'Go Online' and set its onClick prop to {handleOnline}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Go Online' appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the handleOnline function.
successCriteria: A <button> element with the text 'Go Online' is added inside the container div, and its onClick prop is set to {handleOnline}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the button, but make sure to set its onClick prop to {handleOnline} so it triggers the function when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly set up. Check that you've added a <button> with the text 'Go Online' and wired its onClick to the handleOnline function.

steps.title: Add the Go Offline button
steps.instruction: Add a second button with the text 'Go Offline' and wire its onClick event to call the handleOffline function.
steps.hint: Place the new button after the existing 'Go Online' button. Use the same onClick pattern as the first button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a second button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleAction}>Perform Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have two buttons: 'Go Online' and 'Go Offline', both wired to their respective handlers.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Go Offline' is present and its onClick attribute calls handleOffline.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check that the text is 'Go Offline' and onClick calls handleOffline.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Go Offline button is missing or not wired correctly.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Add `export default App;` at the end of the file, after the component definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The file ends with `export default App;` or `export default App` (with semicolon optional).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the App component as the default export.
steps.feedbackWrong: The export statement is missing or incorrect. Add `export default App;` at the end of the file.
